questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.**

If I was he, (1)/ I wouldn't (2)/ accept this gift. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• A wish, a regret, unlikely condition and contrary to fact statements are expressed in **subjunctive mood**.
 
• It is denoted by these key words given below in the table:
 
 
• Wish
 
• **If**
 
• As if
 
• As though
 
 
 
• **Past Conditional tense (were)** is used in the case of subjunctive mood.
 
 
• For example: I **wish **I **were** a king.
 
 
 
• Similarly, in this context, a **subjunctive mood** is introduced here by the use of** 'If**'.
 
• Hence, 'were' must replace 'was' to make the sentence grammatically correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is: *If I **were **he, I wouldn't accept this gift.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Ritesh could succeed (1)/ in catching the Frisbee before (2)/ it reaches the boundary line. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution: The error lies in part 3 of the sentence as the verb ‘reaches’ in simple present tense must be replaced with the verb ‘reached’ in simple past tense. The sentence talks about an incident that had taken place in the past so the verb should be ‘reached.’

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Madhuri did not reply (1)/ when I asked her (2)/ why was she weeping. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution: The error lies in part 3 of the sentence as the structure has been incorrect. In statements the pronoun should be placed before the verb. Thus ‘she’ should be written before ‘was’. It should read as:’why she was weeping.’

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Roshni said that she prefers (1)/ a white shirt than coloured one (2)/ in formal meetings. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution: The error lies in part 2 of the sentence as the preposition ‘than’ is not used with ‘prefer’ and ‘to’ should be used with ‘prefers.’ The article ‘a’ should be used before the word ‘coloured.’ It should read as:’a white shirt than a coloured one.’

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

Nitin told Rohan that he ______ English fluently and was very happy.
questions.solution: The sentence is constructed in simple past tense thus ‘could’, the past tense of ‘can’ should be used here. Thus option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

Sunita told me that she ______ go to Chennai next month.
questions.solution: The sentence is constructed in simple past tense and it talks about a past activity thus ‘would’, the past tense of ‘will’ should be used here. ‘Will’ is incorrect here as the person had said in the past that she was about to go to Chennai.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

The dinner ______ prepared yet when our guests arrived.
questions.solution: The sentence is in past tense thus options 2 and 4 are eliminated first as they are in present tense.The word ‘yet’ makes option 3 eliminate as well. Option 1 is correct as past perfect tense fits here correctly. It is used to refer to a time earlier than before now.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

How much money ______ since the death of your father?
questions.solution: The sentence talks about an activity that is still going on so present perfect tense fits here. The correct structure is the usage of ‘have’ before the pronoun ‘you.’ Thus option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

They treated us not only to cocktails but also ______ dinner.
questions.solution: Someone treats ‘to’ an item thus option 4 is the correct preposition. The other prepositions are incorrect here.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given.**

Grisly
questions.solution:
The word ‘grisly’ means ‘causing horror or disgust.’. The meanings of the words are:

Pleasing=> satisfying or appealing.

Unforgiving=> not willing to forgive or excuse people's faults or wrongdoings

Gruesome=> horrendous or disgusting

Sincerity=> seriousness

Thus option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given.**

questions.solution:
The word ‘interdiction’ means ‘the action of prohibiting or forbidding something.’. The meanings of the other words are:

Decree=> an official order that has the force of law.

Privilege=> special right

Emerge=> move out of or away from something and become visible

Obscene=> offensive or disgusting by accepted standards of morality and decency.

Thus option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question:

Manifest=> to show something clearly, through signs or actions

Obscure=> hidden

Apt=> appropriate

Thus option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question:

Resurrect=>revive or revitalize (something that is inactive, disused, or forgotten

Thus option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given.**

Frantic

Thus option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given.**

Passivity
questions.solution:
The word ‘passivity’ means ‘acceptance of what happens, without active response or resistance.’. The meanings of the words are:

Distinct=> recognizably different in nature from something else of a similar type

Interest=> the feeling of wanting to know or learn about something or someone.

Disregard=> pay no attention to; ignore.

Lucid=> clearly expressed and easy to understand, or (of a person) thinking or speaking clearly

Thus option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question:

questions.solution:

Impede=> to make it more difficult for something to happen or more difficult for someone to do something

Servile=> too eager to serve and please someone else in a way that shows you do not have much respect for yourself

Thus option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given.**

Esoteric
questions.solution:
The word ‘esoteric’ means ‘difficult to understand’. The meanings of the words are:

Obscure=> difficult to understand

Abstruse=> difficult to understand

Familiar=> same

Secret=> private

Thus option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question:

To cut the crackle
questions.solution: The idiom ‘to cut the crackle’ means ‘to stop talking and start’. Thus option 1 is the correct answer.

allowance made to a lady for her expenses

questions.question:

questions.question:

questions.question:

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

Nisha took a longer time to read the proposal for she wanted to (go about it carefully).
questions.solution: The correct phrase here should be ‘go through’ which means ‘read carefully.’ It justifies why the person took a longer time to read the proposal. The other options do not convey any meaning.

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

Why (did you not threw) the clothes away?
questions.solution: The verb must always be in simple present tense when used with ‘did.’ Only option 2 fits here. The other options are grammatically incorrect.

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

Rohit asked Ankit (that why he was) unwilling to go with Suraj.
questions.solution: The error in the phrase is the usage of the word ‘that’. It is never used after the verb ‘asked.’ The structure of the sentence should be:’Rohit asked Ankit why he was unwilling to go with Suraj.’ The pronoun should come before the verb thus option 2 is incorrect. Option 3 is thus the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

Anshika (held) a party when she got her L.L.B. degree.
questions.solution: The word ‘gave’ means ‘throw a party.’ The sentence states that the person achieved something thus option 1 is correct here. The other words are not very apt in the context.

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

You should visit Jaisalmer when you (had been to) Rajasthan.
questions.solution: The correct tense here should be simple present as the sentence talks about a future activity. Thus option 3 is the correct answer. The other options do not fit here.

questions.question:

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which is the best substitute of the phrase.**

Person who gives written testimony for use in a law court
questions.solution:
The meanings of the words are:

Reticence=> reserve

Masochist=> a person who derives sexual gratification from their own pain or humiliation.

Deponent=> a person who makes a deposition or affidavit under oath.

Thus option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which is the best substitute of the phrase.**

One who believes that everything is pre-destined
questions.solution:
The **correct answer** is **1** i.e. '**fatalist**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Lets' look at the meanings of the words:
 
 
• '**Fatalist**' means 'someone who feels that no matter what he or she does, the outcome will be the same because it's predetermined'.
 
• '**Astrologer**' refers to a 'person who uses astrology to tell others about their character or to predict their future'.
 
• '**Hypocrite**' is 'someone who pretends to be something else'.
 
• '**Prodigal**' means 'someone who is spending money or using resources freely and recklessly; wastefully extravagant'. 
 
 
 
• From the above, it is clear that the **phrase 'One who believes that everything is pre-destined' can be substituted by the word 'fatalist'.**

questions.question: health benefits-form ______ bodies
questions.solution: The word here must have a positive meaning as the sentence states that regular physical activity has benefits. Thus ‘leaner’ which means ‘slim’ is the correct answer. ‘Skinny’ means ‘very thin’ and cannot be used here. ‘Static’ means ‘stagnant’ and ‘unhealthier’ means ‘sick.’

questions.question: and ______ blood pressure to improve
questions.solution: Blood pressure should be normal thus ‘lower’ fits better here than ‘higher.’ The other words cannot fit here. ‘Measurable’ means ‘that which can be measured’ and ‘significant’ means ‘notable.’ Thus option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question: the school ______ education programme promotes
questions.solution: The passage talks about physical health thus the kind of education programme should be ‘physical.’ The other words do not fit here as they are not relevant to the topic.

questions.question: an important key to ______ health and well-being
questions.solution: The word ‘curb’ means ‘destroy’ and it does not fit here as no one wants to hamper health. It is not a thing to ‘intensify’ as well. ‘Intensify’ means ‘extend in degree.’ ‘Suppress’ means ‘forcibly put an end to’ and this too does not fit here. The word ‘influence’ means ‘to affect’ and conveys the meaning that the programmes affect health and well-being of people.

questions.question: the design and ______ of school-based
questions.solution: The word ‘delivery’ fits here as ‘design’ and ‘development’ would be repetitive here. ‘Develop’ means ‘form and improve’. ‘Delivery’ means ‘providing or supplying’. The other words too do not fit here.

questions.question: Why student unrest is considered as a global phenomenon of today?

options.text: They are the hope of tomorrow.
Students tend to run away from their responsibilities very often.
Students are being pampered a lot now-a-days.

questions.solution: It is mentioned in the passage ‘Students are the hope of tomorrow and yet, student unrest is a global phenomenon of today.’ Thus option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question: What disease is being talked about in a passage?
questions.solution: The rebelling attitude of the students is considered to be a disease. Thus student unrest is the disease being talked about in the passage.

questions.question: What the students of today do away with?
questions.solution: The passage states that the students want to get rid of the old systems and ways and want to establish their own ways. All the options are mentioned in the passage. Thus option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question: What can be the suitable title for the passage?

options.text: Students – Effective antidote to transform today's world

questions.solution: The passage is focused on the global phenomenon of student unrest. It talks about the consequences and the reasons of the problem. Thus option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question: According to the passage, which of the following is INCORRECT?

options.text: Student unrest is a global phenomenon.
Students are the hope of tomorrow.
Students believe in a new order of things.
Students believe in the values and morality of the older generation.

questions.solution: It is mentioned in the passage ‘*The youthful student wants to break the taboos set by the society and does not believe in the values and morality of the older generation*.’ Thus option 4 is the correct answer.
